question: A copper wire has resistance R. If its radius is reduced to half while keeping the length constant, what will be the new resistance?
solution:
The correct answer is __4R**(Option 2)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Resistance (R)__ of a wire is given by the formula: **R = ρ × (L / A)**, where:
 
• **ρ** is the resistivity of the material, **L** is the length, and **A** is the cross-sectional area.
 
• If the radius is reduced to half, the new radius **r'** becomes **r/2**.
